title: How much canal does the team make in a week?
description: A team makes one kilometre of a water canal in eight days, and the video finds the canal made in one day and in a week by dividing first and then multiplying, the same way as the example in the book. It ends by checking that eight days make the whole kilometre.
teaching_notes: One idea: one day is one of the equal parts, so divide first, and then multiply by the number of days. Watch for students who write eight at the top instead of at the bottom.

source: A team of workers can make 1 km of a water canal in 8 days. So, in one day, the team can make ___ km of the water canal. If they work 5 days a week, they can make ___ km of the water canal in a week.
video_script.why: The child has seen a whole number times a fraction and now divides one whole into equal parts first, then multiplies for a week.
video_script.substitution: One kilometre cut into eight equal parts has one part for each day, so five days take five parts.
video_script.anchor: A team makes one kilometre of canal in eight days: how much in one day and in five days?
video_script.payoff_line: The team makes one eighth of a kilometre in one day and five eighths in a week

final_answer.value: 1/8 km in one day and 5/8 km in a week
final_answer.spoken: one eighth of a kilometre in one day and five eighths of a kilometre in a week

video_script.fraction_reading: one eighth, five eighths, eight eighths
maths_rules: 1 km in 8 days, so 1 day = 1 ÷ 8 = 1/8 km
video_script.design: One idea: divide the whole into equal parts for one day, then multiply for more days. The strip of one kilometre cut into eight parts is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a strip for 1 km of a water canal with a team of workers; a clock of 8 days; question marks for 1 day and for 5 days

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.team: the strip of canal, the team of workers and the 8 days appear
marks.ask: the question marks for one day and for five days appear

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a team of workers.
<bookmark mark='team'/>The team can make one kilometre of a water canal in eight days.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much canal does the team make in one day? And how much if they work five days a week?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a strip for one kilometre of canal is cut into eight equal parts; one part is lit as the work of one day

marks.canal: the strip for one kilometre of canal is drawn
marks.cut: the strip is cut into eight equal parts
marks.day: one part lights up as the work of one day

narration: <bookmark mark='canal'/>Picture one kilometre of the water canal as a long strip.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>The team finishes it in eight days, so cut the strip into eight equal parts.
<bookmark mark='day'/>Each part is the work of one day.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 km of canal in 8 days; the team works 5 days a week

marks.given: the given lines are written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the team makes one kilometre of canal in eight days.
The team works five days a week.

beats.on_screen: To find: canal made in 1 day and in 1 week

marks.find: the find line is written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the canal made in one day and in a week.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: canal in 1 day = 1 km ÷ 8 = 1/8 km

marks.one: the line for one day is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, find the canal made in one day.
<bookmark mark='div'/>One day is one of eight equal parts, so divide one kilometre by eight.
One divided by eight is one eighth of a kilometre.

marks.five: the line for five days is written

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step two, find the canal made in five days.
Five days is five times the work of one day.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply five by one eighth, the same way as the example in your book.
Each piece keeps its size, and we count five pieces.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (check): 8 days = 8 × 1/8 = 8/8 = 1 km, the whole canal

marks.less: 5 days is marked as fewer than 8 days on the strip

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, check by putting the work of one day back in the question.
Eight days of one eighth each make eight eighths, which is the whole kilometre.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Five days are fewer than eight days. The answer for five days must be less than one kilometre.

marks.one: 1/8 km is written and boxed for one day
marks.five: 5 × 1/8 = 5/8 km is written and boxed for a week
marks.pay: both answers stay on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>In one day, the canal grows by one eighth of a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five times one eighth is five eighths.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The team makes one eighth of a kilometre in one day and five eighths in a week.
